units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Solve both sign branches and verify branch restrictions against the nonnegative modulus.
units.summary: Solve a linear modulus equation algebraically.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Use positivity, the vertical-axis intercept and monotonic exponential growth to draw the supplied function.
units.summary: Sketch a simple exponential graph.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Take logarithms of 4^x=100 and round the resulting input.
units.summary: Solve a numerical exponential equation.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Generate the alternating terms to prove periodicity, then reuse their unprinted pair values and period to sum 85 terms.
units.summary: Identify a periodic recurrence and sum an odd number of terms.

exceptions: The raw (a)(ii) 2-mark tariff jointly covers the periodicity demonstration and the order in (a)(i),(ii).

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Expand the forward difference quotient for 2x² and take its limit as the increment tends to zero.
units.summary: Differentiate a quadratic from first principles.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Apply the trapezium rule to all five ordinates, then reuse its unprinted estimate with logarithm power and product laws to transform two related integrals.
units.summary: Estimate related logarithmic integrals from a trapezium calculation.

exceptions: The raw (b)(ii) 3-mark tariff jointly covers both related integrals. Source rendering confirms log₃((2x)^10) and log₃(18x), rather than a tenth power of the logarithm.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate the supplied sine function, use the sketch to select the correct stationary maximum and reuse the unprinted derivative for one Newton–Raphson step.
units.summary: Locate a specified trigonometric maximum and refine a root.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the two function values explicitly printed before (b) and continuity to identify a sign change.
units.summary: Justify a bracket for a continuous-function root.

exceptions: Visually verified f(x)=8sin(x/2)−3x+9; the marked local maximum P is the later maximum shown on the sketch. Parts (a),(c) are grouped to retain the derivative; (b) is scored separately and uses only supplied values.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Factor out the leading constant, obtain four rational-power terms and reuse their signs to infer the direction of the truncated-series error.
units.summary: Expand a radical binomial and judge approximation error.

exceptions: Visually verified: the binomial is √(4−9x), and the approximation substitutes x=1/9 to estimate √3.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Expand the numerator over 4√x, integrate the resulting powers between the two positive intercepts and reverse the sign because the curve lies below the axis.
units.summary: Find an exact area under a rational-power curve.

exceptions: Visually verified denominator 4√x; standard power integration suffices, without partial fractions or integration by parts.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the maximum for amplitude, the modulus period for angular rate and the increasing initial branch to select the phase.
units.summary: Fit a modulus-sine Ferris-wheel height model.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Recognise that the passenger remains above ground at the minimum, so a positive vertical offset improves the model; no fitted parameters are needed.
units.summary: Refine a Ferris-wheel height model’s baseline.

exceptions: Visually verified H=|A sin(bt+α)°|; extraction corrupts the modulus bars. The graph shows a rising initial branch and a full revolution corresponding to the modulus period.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Set the supplied rational function equal to 3/2 and solve for the input.
units.summary: Evaluate an inverse rational function at a supplied output.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Determine the unprinted rational decomposition, identify the inverse function’s range and reuse these results to bound f(g⁻¹(x)).
units.summary: Rearrange a rational function and find an inverse-composite range.

exceptions: Visually verified f(x)=(8x+5)/(2x+3), x>−3/2, and the input in (a) is 3/2. The defined g has domain [0,4].

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed Year 1/AS skill scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Separate the even and odd cases, substitute algebraic parity forms and show the product is even in each exhaustive case.
units.summary: Prove an integer expression is even.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Apply the quotient rule, determine the unprinted positive factor g(x), then use it to reduce the stationary-point condition to a quadratic discriminant inequality.
units.summary: Differentiate a rational exponential and constrain stationary-point parameters.

exceptions: Source denominator is 4x²+k with k>0. Parts are grouped because showing that g(x) has no zeros is needed to justify using only the printed quadratic factor for stationary points.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use proportional three-dimensional displacement components to find the point parameter, then reuse the point to construct the parallel direction and calculate the exact distance.
units.summary: Determine collinear points and an extended position-vector distance.

exceptions: The mark scheme reuses p from (a) in the vector to D; parts are grouped to retain that unprinted parameter.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Find the unprinted partial-fraction coefficients, separate variables and integrate, then apply the supplied time-volume observation to determine the integration constant.
units.summary: Use partial fractions to solve an oxygen-production differential equation.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the explicit solution printed in (b) to identify its zero-volume start and long-time limit, converting the delay from hours to minutes.
units.summary: Interpret a differential-equation model’s delay and limiting volume.

exceptions: Visually verified dV/dt=3V/((2t−1)(t+1)) and the printed solution V=3(2t−1)/(t+1). The raw (c)(ii) 2-mark tariff jointly covers delay and limiting volume.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Equate consecutive geometric ratios and use tan(θ)=sin(θ)/cos(θ) with the Pythagorean identity to obtain the printed quadratic.
units.summary: Derive a trigonometric condition for geometric-series terms.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Solve the quadratic explicitly printed in (a), select the exact obtuse radian angle and reuse it to determine the signed first term, convergent ratio and simplified infinite sum.
units.summary: Find an obtuse series angle and its exact sum to infinity.

exceptions: Visually verified series terms 12cos(θ), 5+2sin(θ), 6tan(θ) and requested sum k(1−√3); (b),(c) are grouped because the selected angle is not printed.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate both parameter expressions, evaluate the gradient and coordinates at π/4, then construct the perpendicular line.
units.summary: Find a normal to a trigonometric parametric curve.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use sec²(t)=1+tan²(t) with the supplied x expression to establish the printed Cartesian equation.
units.summary: Eliminate a tangent parameter to obtain a parabola.

units.introduced_year_basis: Assessed additional A level skill scope, beyond the AS subset.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the Cartesian equation explicitly printed in (b), require two distinct real intersections and impose the x interval induced by the parameter bounds; the discriminant condition alone is insufficient.
units.summary: Constrain a line to meet a restricted parametric parabola twice.

exceptions: Visually verified x=2tan(t)+1, y=2sec²(t)+3 and −π/4≤t≤π/3. Part (c) must retain the parameter interval as well as the printed Cartesian equation from (b).
